land.text: central Somalia; the page lists the Hiraab Imamate as a predecessor without naming land

predecessors.note: The Hobyo page's infobox lists the Hiraab Imamate as a predecessor. The Hiraab Imamate page (opened in the reviewer round): 'a Somali kingdom that ruled parts of the Horn of Africa' with infobox 'Established: late 17th century', 'Disestablished: 7 January 1889' (Sultan Abiker's treaty with Italy, 7 January 1889), capital Mogadishu, land 'from Mogadishu in the Banaadir province, through the Shabelle valley and Galguduud, to the arid lands of Mudug', which 'included the port of Hobyo'; it lists the Sultanate of Hobyo, the Sultanate of the Geledi and Italian Somaliland as successors. The page names no date or border for the part Hobyo took, so the land stays Cliopatria's 1880 shape (no Cliopatria row for the Imamate; a dossier is needed).

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the Majeerteen page dates the establishment of Hobyo to 1878, two years before Cliopatria's first shape (1880). The 1880 shape is used for 1878-1879.

134,617 km2. The page gives no infobox area, so the area check is impossible; it says 'present-day central and northeastern Somalia, and eastern Ethiopia' and the shape (45.37-49.66E, 3.31-7.68N) covers central Somalia with about 22,000 km2 in Ethiopia. The page names no town but Hobyo; the shape is unverified beyond that.

107,741 km2: the 1880 shape less about 27,000 km2 on the south-west (134,617 - 107,741 = 26,876 km2). The cause is on no page opened (ledger 1890, confidence 1). The shape stands as Cliopatria's; from 8 February 1889 Hobyo is an Italian protectorate, which changes the status, not the drawn borders.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria ends the Hobyo row in 1894 and covers the land with Italian Africa from 1895, but the sultan reigned until 1925 and the page says it was integrated into Italian Somaliland only after the Campaign of the Sultanates. The 1890 shape is extended to 1899 (the part in eastern Ethiopia is cut from 1900, see sultanate-of-hobyo_1900); the pages are silent on its borders in these years (confidence 1).

correction.text: the 1890 shape without the land that Cliopatria's Ethiopian Empire shape of 1900 holds (the eastern Ethiopian part, 91 H3 res-5 cells, about 23,000 km2): Hobyo as an Italian protectorate until the deposition of 1925

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (reviewer fix): the 1890 shape carried into 1895-1925 contains 91 H3 res-5 cells (about 23,000 km2) that lie inside the ethiopian-empire dossier's 1900 and 1908 shapes (grid overlap of Cliopatria's Hobyo 1890 and Ethiopian Empire 1900/1908 shapes: 91 cells; with the 1898 shape 0), so two dossiers would draw the same land from 1900. The Hobyo page, re-read, says only 'eastern Ethiopia' in its lead and names no Ethiopian border, no Ethiopian claim and no Ogaden or Haud land of Hobyo; the ethiopian-empire dossier (af-01-b) has the Ogaden occupied from 1891 (its ledger/39, from 'nobody') and its 1900 shape reaches 47.9 E. Decision: the shared land goes to the Ethiopian Empire from 1900 (ledger 1900 loss, confidence 1, bridged from the shape overlap, page silent); the Hobyo dossier keeps the rest of the 1890 shape. If af-01-b dates its Ogaden gain otherwise, this cut should move with it.

region.text: central and northeastern Somalia, and eastern Ethiopia

ledger.note: 1878: Yusuf Ali Kenadid founds the Sultanate of Hobyo in central Somalia. The Majeerteen page: he 'helped establish the separate Sultanate of Hobyo in 1878'; the Hobyo page says only 'established between the 1870s and 1884'; Cliopatria draws it from 1880. The page places it in 'present-day central and northeastern Somalia, and eastern Ethiopia'.

region.text: the southern edge of the Majeerteen shape trimmed when Cliopatria begins Hobyo in 1880 (about 760 km2)

ledger.note: 1878: a southern strip of the Majeerteen shape goes to Hobyo (about 760 km2). Neither page names the land; the region is the strip by which Cliopatria's Majeerteen shape shrinks when it begins Hobyo in 1880.

8 February 1889: Hobyo becomes an Italian protectorate. The infobox: 'Protectorate treaty with the Kingdom of Italy: 8 February 1889'; the text says Hobyo became a protectorate in 1889 and Boqor Osman signed a similar agreement the following year (the Majeerteen page gives 7 April 1889). Kenadid refused the Italians' request to let a British contingent land. The status change does not alter the drawn borders.

region.text: the south-western part of the 1880 shape absent from the 1890 shape

ledger.note: 1890: Cliopatria's shape loses about 27,000 km2 on the south-west (134,617 - 107,741 = 26,876 km2) (45.96-49.48E, 3.4-7.64N), where its Italian Africa row begins. Neither page names the land or the year (page silent); the event bridges the shape change.

region.text: the eastern Ethiopian part of the 1890 shape, inside Cliopatria's Ethiopian Empire shape of 1900

ledger.note: 1900: the part of Hobyo's shape in eastern Ethiopia (91 H3 res-5 cells, about 23,000 km2) passes to the Ethiopian Empire, whose Cliopatria shape reaches 47.9 E from 1900 (the Ogaden occupied from 1891 per the ethiopian-empire dossier). The Hobyo page says only 'eastern Ethiopia' and dates and names no cession or border (page silent); the year and the land are bridged from the grid overlap, to keep two dossiers from drawing the same land. The ethiopian-empire dossier (af-01-b) carries the Ogaden gain from 'nobody'; it should name sultanate-of-hobyo as counterpart for this strip from 1900.

region.text: the Sultanate of Hobyo without the part in eastern Ethiopia held by the Ethiopian Empire

ledger.note: 1 October 1925: Italian columns enter Hobyo and depose the sultan. 'Three dubat columns under Colonel Di Bello entered the sultanate and occupied it completely within a few weeks, deposing the ruler'; Omar Samatar's revolt took El Buur on 9 November 1925 and the Italians retook it on 26 December 1925.

region.text: the Sultanate of Hobyo without the part in eastern Ethiopia held by the Ethiopian Empire

ledger.note: October 1925: the Sultanate of Hobyo ends with the deposition of Sultan Ali Yusuf Kenadid. The Hobyo page dates the integration into Italian Somaliland to 1927 ('Campaign of the Sultanates and disintegration of the Sultanate of Hobyo' 1927); the reign list ends in 1925.

wars.name: Campaign of the Sultanates

zones.text: the Sultanate of Hobyo (without its eastern Ethiopian part), occupied from 1 October 1925

wars.outcome: Italian victory: Hobyo is occupied 'completely within a few weeks' from 1 October 1925 and its ruler deposed; Omar Samatar's revolt takes El Buur (9 November 1925) and is crushed by 26 December 1925; the sultanate is integrated into Italian Somaliland.
wars.note: In September 1925 Sultan Ali Yusuf Kenadid agreed to hand over his weapons. The Hobyo page's infobox dates the disintegration to 1927.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line: the 1889 treaty fixes no frontier on the page; the borders are Cliopatria's approximations.

notes: Page budget 1-2 pages, two opened for this state (Hobyo, Campaign of the Sultanates); the Majeerteen page, opened for the neighbouring dossier, is cited for the 1878 date. Cliopatria ends the Hobyo row in 1894 and covers the land with Italian Africa from 1895, while the pages say the sultan reigned as an Italian protégé until October 1925; the dossier extends the 1890 shape to 1925 (new keyframe, confidence 1) and records the 8 February 1889 treaty as a 'rename' event, the schema having no type for 'becomes a protectorate' in the vassal's own dossier. The Italian Africa dossier should carry a vassal_start 8 February 1889 and a vassal_end October 1925 with counterpart sultanate-of-hobyo. Disagreements: founding 1878 (Majeerteen page), 'between the 1870s and 1884' (Hobyo page), 1880 (Cliopatria); end 1925 (deposition, Campaign page and reign list) against 1927 (Hobyo infobox and text); Majeerteen treaty 7 April 1889 against Hobyo 8 February 1889 with Boqor Osman signing 'the following year' (Hobyo page). Kenadid's rank as 1854-1912 conflicts with the 1870s founding. The 27,000 km2 loss in 1890 (26,876 km2 by shapes.csv) and the Ethiopian part of the shape are unexplained by the pages. Not on the pages: the Hiraab Imamate (a predecessor), the dispute near Warsheikh with Zanzibar (undated), Kenadid's exile to Aden and Eritrea (undated). Counterparts needing dossiers: hiraab-imamate. Gazetteer names needed: Hobyo (place). Reviewer round (af-01-c-fixed): the 1895 keyframe now ends in 1899 and a new keyframe sultanate-of-hobyo_1900 (1900..1925) removes the 91 H3 res-5 cells (about 23,000 km2) of eastern Ethiopia that Cliopatria's Ethiopian Empire shapes of 1900 and 1908 also hold (ledger 1900 loss to ethiopian-empire, confidence 1); the Hobyo page, re-read, names no Ethiopian border. Counterpart note for af-01-b: the ethiopian-empire ledger/39 (Ogaden from 'nobody', 1891) should name sultanate-of-hobyo as counterpart for that strip from 1900. Area figures in the 1890 loss corrected to 26,876 km2. Hiraab Imamate page opened in the reviewer round (see identity.predecessors): late 17th century to 7 January 1889, capital Mogadishu; a dossier hiraab-imamate is still needed (no Cliopatria row). The Italian Somaliland page (the 1890 loss and the protectorate borders) was not opened in this round.
